_info: Points de grammaire. Formats : ["q", phrase, choix, bonne, explication] · ["e", phrase, index du mot faux, correction, explication] · ["v", phrase, vrai?, correction, explication] · ["o", phrase, traduction]

points.titre: A, an, the et le pluriel
points.fiche:
a ou an ?

On regarde le son, pas la lettre :

a car · a university (son « you ») · an apple · an hour (h muet)

Pas d'article pour les généralités

I love music. · Cats are cute. (J'adore la musique.)

Mais un métier prend toujours a/an : She is a doctor.

Le pluriel

car → cars · box → boxes · city → cities

Irréguliers : man → men, woman → women, child → children, person → people, foot → feet
items: « apple » commence par un son voyelle → an.
Métier → a/an obligatoire : She is a doctor.
Le h de « hour » ne se prononce pas → an.
Généralité → pas d'article : I love music.
« teacher » commence par un son consonne → a.

points.fiche:
I → memy → mine
you → youyour → yours
he → himhis → his
she → herher → hers
it → itits
we → usour → ours
they → themtheir → theirs

Son / sa : ça dépend du propriétaire !

Tom and his sister · Sarah and her brother

En français, on regarde l'objet (son frère, sa sœur). En anglais, on regarde à qui il appartient.

💡 its (son, pour une chose) n'a pas d'apostrophe. it's = it is.
items: Après le verbe → pronom complément : me.
Seul, à la fin → mine (le mien).
Me and Paul live in Lyon.
En sujet → « Paul and I live… ».
Devant un nom → their (theirs s'emploie seul).
its = son/sa pour une chose ou un animal.

points.resume: il y a + prépositions de lieu
points.fiche:
Il y a

There is a cat. (singulier) · There are two cats. (pluriel)

There isn't any milk. · Are there any shops?

Où ?

indans
onsur
undersous
next toà côté de
betweenentre
behindderrière
in front ofdevant
💡 Ne dis jamais « it has » pour « il y a » : c'est toujours there is / there are.
items: There ___ a cat in the garden.
The bank is next of the station.
Négation au pluriel → there aren't any.
There is a map on the wall.
Il y a un plan sur le mur.

points.fiche:
Adjectif court → -er / the -est

tall → taller than → the tallest

big → bigger · easy → easier

Adjectif long → more / the most

expensive → more expensive → the most expensive

Les irréguliers

good → better → the best · bad → worse → the worst

Égalité : as fast as me

💡 « plus grand que » = bigger than. Jamais « that » !
items: This hotel is ___ than the other one.
It's the ___ day of my life!
She is as fast ___ her sister.
This is the more beautiful city.
Superlatif d'un adjectif long → the most.
He is the best player in the team.
C'est le meilleur joueur de l'équipe.

points.fiche:
many ou much ?

many + ce qui se compte : many cars, many people

much + ce qui ne se compte pas : much money, much time, much water

a lot of marche avec tout.

some ou any ?

some dans une phrase affirmative : I have some friends.

any dans une négation ou une question : I don't have any money. Do you have any questions?

💡 Ces mots ne prennent jamais de « s » : information, advice, news, luggage, furniture.
items: money ne se compte pas → much.
Can you give me some advices?
advice ne prend jamais de s.
There are a lot of people.
a lot of marche avec tout.
I have a few friends in London.

points.fiche:
have / has + participe passé

Il relie le passé au présent :

Expérience : Have you ever been to London? · I've never eaten sushi.

Résultat visible : I've lost my keys!

Ça dure encore : I've lived here for 3 years / since 2021.

for ou since ?

for + une durée (for two hours) · since + un point de départ (since Monday)

💡 « J'habite ici depuis 3 ans » = I have lived here for 3 years. Avec une date précise (yesterday, in 2019), on repasse au prétérit.
items: Depuis + ça dure encore → present perfect.
Have you ever ___ to New York?
She has worked here ___ ten years.
He has lived here since five years.

points.fiche:
canpouvoir, savoir faire
mustdevoir (obligation forte)
have toêtre obligé (règle extérieure)
mustn'tinterdit !
don't have topas obligé
shouldconseil (devrais)
mightpeut-être

La règle d'or

Modal + verbe sans to, sans s : She can swim. You should go.

💡 Attention au piège : mustn't = c'est interdit, mais don't have to = ce n'est pas nécessaire.
items: It's Sunday, you ___ get up early.
You look tired. You ___ go to bed.
Un modal ne prend jamais de s.
Après un modal → forme de base.
You should to see a doctor.
should + verbe sans to : You should see a doctor.
Tu n'es pas obligé de venir.

points.fiche:
Situation possible

If + présent, will + verbe

If it rains, I'll stay home.

Situation imaginaire

If + prétérit, would + verbe

If I had money, I would travel. · If I were you, I'd call her.

💡 Comme en français (« si je serais »), on ne met jamais will ou would juste après if.
items: If it rains, I ___ at home.
If I ___ rich, I would buy a boat.
What would you do if you ___ the lottery?
If I will see him, I'll tell him.
Pas de will après if : If I see him…
If I had time, I will help you.
If I were you, I would call her.
« If I were you » = à ta place.
I would travel if I had more money.
Je voyagerais si j'avais plus d'argent.

points.fiche:
atune heure, un moment : at 8, at noon, at night
onun jour, une date : on Monday, on 3 May, on my birthday
inmois, année, saison, partie de journée : in July, in 2024, in summer, in the morning
💡 Pas de préposition devant this, next, last, every : See you next week. I work every day.
items: in the morning, mais at night.
Pas de préposition avant next : See you next week.
Nous jouons en général la nuit.

points.fiche:
was / were + verbe-ing

Une action en cours dans le passé : c'est le décor.

At 8 pm, I was watching TV.

Souvent interrompue par un prétérit

I was sleeping when the phone rang.

While she was cooking, I set the table.

💡 Pense à un film : le past continuous = la scène qui se déroule, le prétérit = l'événement qui la coupe.
items: Action en cours interrompue → was watching.
While she was cooking, the phone ___.
I was walk home when it started to rain.
It was raining all day yesterday.
Action en cours sur une période passée.
I was sleeping when you called.
Je dormais quand tu as appelé.

points.fiche:
be (au bon temps) + participe passé

présentIt is made in China.
prétéritIt was built in 1900.
present perfectIt has been sold.
futurIt will be done tomorrow.

L'auteur de l'action : by → written by Shakespeare.

💡 On l'utilise beaucoup quand on ne sait pas (ou peu importe) qui fait l'action : My bike was stolen.
items: Passif au futur → will be + participe.
Present perfect passif → has been stolen.
The letter was write by my grandmother.
The windows are cleaned from a company.
My phone was stolen last night.
The match was cancelled because of the rain.
Le match a été annulé à cause de la pluie.

points.fiche:
On recule d'un temps

"I am tired."He said he was tired.
"I will come."She said she would come.
"I can help."He said he could help.

say ou tell ?

She said (that)… · She told me (that)… (tell + quelqu'un)

💡 Dans une question indirecte, plus d'inversion ni de do : He asked where I lived (pas « where did I live »).
items: Pas d'inversion dans une question indirecte.
She said me that she was ill.
say ne prend pas de complément : she told me.
He asked where did I work.
Question indirecte sans did : He asked where I worked.
She said she could help us.
He told me he was hungry.
Il m'a dit qu'il avait faim.

points.fiche:
whopour une personne
whichpour une chose
thatles deux (très courant à l'oral)
whosedont / de qui (possession)
whereoù (un lieu)

The man whose car was stolen… (l'homme dont la voiture…)

💡 Quand le relatif est complément, on peut le supprimer : The film (that) I saw was great.
items: The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.
The car ___ I bought is red.
That's the man ___ son plays for Arsenal.
This is the town ___ I grew up.
The book who I read was great.
The girl which I met was nice.
The film I watched was boring.
The man who called you is my boss.
L'homme qui t'a appelé est mon patron.

points.fiche:
+ -ing

enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, can't stand, look forward to, et après une préposition (for, of, about…)

I enjoy reading. · Thanks for helping me.

+ to

want, decide, hope, need, plan, would like, learn

I want to go. · She decided to stay.

💡 Le sens change avec stop : I stopped smoking (j'ai arrêté de fumer) ≠ I stopped to smoke (je me suis arrêté pour fumer).
items: look forward to + -ing (ici, to est une préposition).
He stopped ___ ten years ago, he doesn't smoke now.
Would you mind closing the window?
I hope to see you soon.

points.titre: Regrets : if I had…, I wish
points.fiche:
Refaire le passé

If + had + participe, would have + participe

If I had known, I would have come. (Si j'avais su, je serais venu.)

I wish

Regret sur le présent → prétérit : I wish I were taller.

Regret sur le passé → past perfect : I wish I had studied more.

💡 Même règle qu'avant : jamais « would » après if. If you had asked (pas « would have asked »).
items: If I had known, I ___ you.
If she ___ earlier, she wouldn't have missed the train.
Regret sur le présent → I wish + prétérit.
I wish I ___ that. I'm sorry.
Regret sur le passé → I wish + past perfect.
If you would have asked, I would have said yes.
Jamais would après if : If you had asked…
I wish I have more free time.
If we had left earlier, we would have caught the bus.
if + had + participe, would have + participe.
If I had studied, I would have passed.
